result.summary: Updates legacy-to-SQLite wallet migration to skip copying legacy records, transactions, and address book entries upfront rather than writing and subsequently deleting them. Address book entries and transactions are instead written directly to their corresponding destination wallets during the migration process. With post-migration record erasure eliminated, several unused wallet database deletion functions (RemoveTxs, EraseTx, DeleteRecordsWithDB, EraseRecords) are removed, and HasLegacyRecords is made static to walletdb.cpp.
result.problem: Legacy wallet migration copies all database records into SQLite, only for migration to immediately erase legacy key/script records, delete unneeded address book entries, and overwrite transaction records. This generates redundant disk I/O during migration and requires maintaining otherwise unused database deletion code paths in the wallet.
evidence: Author description: 'When migrating a legacy wallet, we can skip the records in MigrateToSQLite that we would delete later on during migration... This allows us to remove several database record erase functions, specifically EraseTx and EraseRecords.'
result.changed_since_previous: Added commit 9ef3606adb to also skip copying address book records (DESTDATA, NAME, PURPOSE) during the initial SQLite migration pass and write only relevant entries to target wallets, removing the need for post-migration address book record deletions.
result.card: Modifies legacy wallet migration to SQLite by skipping legacy records, transactions, and address book entries during the initial database record copy rather than writing them and erasing them later. Because migration reconstructs descriptor records, transactions, and address book entries directly, writing and deleting them was redundant. This cleanup eliminates unnecessary database writes during migration and allows the removal of unused wallet record deletion methods, including RemoveTxs and EraseTx. It has no dependencies.

risk.why: A mistake in filtering or selectively writing wallet database records during migration could cause data corruption or loss of transactions and address book entries for users migrating legacy wallets.
